description:
## Why

Under Level 3 OSCAL alignment, each lint IS an OSCAL Control. The Rust `Lint` trait stays for the executable side (checking a cert) but each impl declares its canonical OSCAL Control metadata: id, title, description, parameters, parts, etc. Loading a lint Catalog from an OSCAL JSON file constructs the same set of Controls that hardcoded Lint impls produce.

## What

Extend the `Lint` trait so each implementor declares OSCAL Control metadata:

```rust
pub trait Lint {
    // Existing executable side
    fn check_cert(&self, cert: &Certificate, ctx: &LintContext) -> LintResult;
    
    // New canonical-metadata side
    fn control(&self) -> oscal::Control;
}

// Or alternatively: Lint impls register declaratively into a Catalog,
// and the executable side is keyed by Control id at runtime.
```

Each `oscal::Control` carries:

- `id` — stable identifier (e.g., `rfc5280.crit-ext-must-be-recognized`).
- `title` — short human-readable name.
- `parts` — structured prose: `statement` (the rule), `guidance` (interpretation notes), `assessment-objective` (what passing/failing means).
- `params` — parameters the rule can be tuned by (e.g., max serial length).
- `links` — citations to RFC sections (e.g., `href="rfc5280#section-4.2.1.9"`).

A 'Catalog' is then `Vec<oscal::Control>` corresponding to a set of `Lint` impls. Loading from JSON deserializes a Catalog; pairing with executable Rust code happens by id.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Lint` trait carries a way to obtain the OSCAL Control metadata for each impl.
- [ ] A canonical 'RFC-conformance Catalog' is constructible from `pkix-lint`'s built-in lints.
- [ ] Catalog round-trips: deserialize OSCAL JSON, run lints, get same set of Controls as the hardcoded Catalog.
- [ ] Citation links use `https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/...` URLs or DOI form.
- [ ] At least one lint demonstrates parameter use (e.g., a `max-serial-length` parameter overrideable via OSCAL Profile).

## Depends on

PKIX-9vnx.2 (binding for `oscal::Control`), PKIX-9vnx.3, PKIX-9vnx.4, PKIX-9vnx.5 (the rest of the data model).
notes:
Reframed 2026-05-11 (Arch 2 — see PKIX-ztmr / PKIX-9vnx notes):

- Lint trait grows metadata methods (id, title, description, severity, citation, parameters) — unchanged from original plan.
- The new method shape is NOT `fn control(&self) -> oscal::Control` (that implies an `oscal::Control` Rust type). Instead either:
  (a) discrete trait methods (`fn title(&self) -> &str`, `fn rfc_citation(&self) -> Option<&str>`, etc.) that a serializer composes into OSCAL Control JSON, or
  (b) `fn oscal_control_metadata(&self) -> serde_json::Value` if a lint wants to emit a full custom Control fragment.
- A canonical 'RFC-conformance Catalog' is built by iterating the registered Lints and projecting each one to OSCAL Control JSON via the serializer. The Catalog is materialized as JSON, not as a Rust `oscal::Catalog` struct.
- Round-trip: load Catalog JSON, pair each Control by id with a registered Lint impl, run lints. Acceptance unchanged.
- No longer blocked by PKIX-9vnx.2 (closed).
Decomposed 2026-05-11 by do-beads loop session bd-spin-20260511T170116Z-854030 into 5 children with linear+parallel deps:

- PKIX-9vnx.6.1 (P2) — Lint trait OSCAL-Control metadata methods (foundational). No deps.
- PKIX-9vnx.6.2 (P2) — OSCAL Catalog JSON serializer. Depends on .6.1.
- PKIX-9vnx.6.3 (P2) — OSCAL Catalog round-trip + id-pair runner. Depends on .6.2.
- PKIX-9vnx.6.4 (P2) — Lint parameter mechanism + first parametric Lint (Rfc5280MaxSerialLengthLint). Depends on .6.1. Parallelizable with .6.2 / .6.3.
- PKIX-9vnx.6.5 (P3) — OSCAL Profile modify-directive overrides parameters. Depends on .6.4 and .6.2.

Key context for whichever agent picks up .6.1 first:
- pkix-lint has ZERO RFC-conformance Lint impls today; only the 6 CABF lints (scheduled to move to pkix-lint-cabf via PKIX-amgn.3).
- The Lint trait already has id/citation/severity/scope/applies_to. .6.1 adds title/description/rfc_section_id/rfc_url as defaults.
- No Parameter type exists; .6.4 designs it.
- LintRunner registers via Vec<Box<dyn Lint>>; no id-keyed map exists (.6.3 introduces one).
title: Lint-as-Control mapping: each Lint declares OSCAL Control metadata
